Development Guide

Development Guide#

Prerequisites#

  • Python ≥ 3.13

  • PostgreSQL ≥ 17.5

  • n8n (required for WhatsApp integration)

  • Node.js + npm (for Tailwind CSS build)

Setup#

# masuk ke project
cd b-snap

Buat virtual environment#

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate   # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

install dependencies#

pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements.txt

Frontend (Tailwind CSS)#

# install dependencies (once)
npm install -D tailwindcss@3.4.1 postcss autoprefixer

# run watcher (rebuild CSS on change)
npm run dev

Tips#

Simpan .env untuk variabel seperti DB connection, API key, dsb.

Jangan commit .env → tambahkan ke .gitignore.

Gunakan pre-commit hooks (optional) untuk linting/formatting sebelum push. “””

Database initialization#

Before starting web or scheduler directly, apply migrations and seed missing configuration keys on the development PostgreSQL database:

python -m app.db.migrate

On Windows, start-local.ps1 web, dev, and all run this command before starting services; start-local.ps1 migrate runs it on its own. Failures stop startup. Direct uvicorn/Gunicorn startup never creates tables or runs migrations.

Migration integration tests require an isolated PostgreSQL test database via BSNAP_TEST_DATABASE_URL. They create and drop unique temporary schemas and use disposable schemas independently of the shared database fixture:

python -m pytest app/tests/test_database_migration.py -o addopts="" -q

Safe automated tests (CA-12)#

Run from the repository root with the project Python environment:

python -m pytest --collect-only -q
python -m pytest -q

pytest.ini is the single configuration source. Test bootstrap overrides DATABASE_URL with a disabled loopback address before importing application code; application-engine connections and unmocked external DNS/socket connections fail. Loopback servers used by mocked transport tests remain available. HTTP client fixtures use ASGITransport without starting application lifespan, scheduler or capture workers. Tests requiring actual lifecycle behavior must mock their transports and database explicitly.

Mocked/unit tests run without PostgreSQL. Database cases skip with an explicit reason unless the operator supplies a dedicated disposable test PostgreSQL:

$env:BSNAP_TEST_DATABASE_URL = 'postgresql+psycopg2://bsnap_test@127.0.0.1:55432/bsnap_test'
$env:BSNAP_TEST_POSTGRES_URL = $env:BSNAP_TEST_DATABASE_URL
python -m pytest -q

Supply credentials through the local environment when required. Never use the application DATABASE_URL for this command. The test user must be able to create and drop schemas. Shared ORM tests create a unique pytest_<uuid> schema, retain PostgreSQL JSONB and audit triggers, and wrap each test in an outer transaction with session savepoints; application commits are rolled back at teardown. Migration and concurrency tests create their own unique schemas. All schemas are dropped on successful or failed test teardown. Hard termination can require removing the identified disposable schemas manually. Parallel runs must use separate schemas; do not point concurrent jobs at application data.

The shared ORM fixture uses model DDL; separate migration tests exercise Alembic upgrade/downgrade against PostgreSQL. Passing unit tests without the explicit PostgreSQL URLs does not validate migrations, triggers or concurrency.

Legacy manual diagnostics#

Eight historical scripts now live under scripts/diagnostics/, outside pytest’s test paths. Importing them does not run their old module-level operations. They are retained as manual legacy tools, not automated tests or current operational recipes. Some reference container-only paths or old APIs; inspect them first. They may read/modify deployment data or send notifications when explicitly run:

python -m scripts.diagnostics.group_access --allow-live-operations

The flag is mandatory even for read-only legacy checks. Automated tests never invoke that flag. No real SMTP, GoWA, camera capture or production scheduler is required by the automated suite.
